column1: # Known one-name-two-slots collisions, the backlog find_name_collisions.py --check tolerates.
# A row is a defect not yet fixed, or one of the few shapes the detector still misreads (a refcount
# assignment `a = b` puts the RHS first in both the code and the ordered pairing, so the two
# names can swap). Neither is a decision that the row is acceptable.
# Remove the row when the name is split; never add one to silence a new collision.
# 2026-08-29, fix-routed-leftovers: g_btn_play (0x00C66798 / 0x00C685C8) and g_prg_energy
# (0x00C66790 / 0x00C68628) REMOVED -- TScreen_MatchPrep.CreateScreen now spells its own two
# slots g_matchprep_btnplay and g_matchprep_prgenergy, the names its own SetUpScreen already
# reads them by, and extracted/global_alias_overrides.tsv carries the two rows that stop the
# generated tables sending those names back to the colliding ones. Measured with
# find_name_collisions.py before and after the change: 30 -> 28 collisions found, exactly
# those two gone (plus g_training_state, which the detector stops misreading once the
# 0x00C5B208 alias rows land), and NOTHING added.
